skill.name: baseline-ui
skill.description: Applies an opinionated UI baseline for frontend polish, accessibility, animation, typography, layout, and Tailwind CSS usage.
skill.summary: Reviews frontend UI work against a concise baseline for cleaner, more accessible interfaces.
skill.author: ibelick

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The file is Markdown guidance for frontend UI review, and the flagged backticks are inline formatting rather than executable commands.

remediation.issue: Inline backticks resemble executable shell syntax to static analysis.
remediation.suggestion: Keep Markdown examples descriptive and avoid command-like formatting when a plain text label is sufficient.

remediation.issue: External documentation link may be treated as a network indicator.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that the Base UI URL is a reference link only and does not require the agent to fetch content.

- MUST use a fixed `z-index` scale (no arbitrary `z-*`)
- SHOULD use `size-*` for square elements instead of `w-*` + `h-*`
- NEVER animate large `blur()` or `backdrop-filter` surfaces
- NEVER apply `will-change` outside an active animation
- NEVER use `useEffect` for anything that can be expressed as render logic

- SHOULD avoid animating large images or full-screen surfaces

content.user_title: Polish Frontend UI with Baseline Rules
content.value_statement: AI-generated interfaces often miss spacing, accessibility, motion, and layout details. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused UI review checklist.
actual_capabilities: Applies a frontend UI checklist covering stack, components, interaction, animation, typography, layout, performance, and visual design.
Reviews a specified file and reports violations with a short reason and concrete fix suggestion.
Promotes Tailwind CSS defaults, existing component primitives, accessible controls, and clear empty states.
Constrains animation to requested motion, compositor properties, short durations, and reduced-motion support.
Flags common AI UI issues such as blocked paste, unsafe viewport sizing, arbitrary z-index values, and unnecessary gradients.
limitations: It provides review guidance and does not run automated design tests.
It assumes Tailwind CSS and modern React-style component workflows.
It cannot verify visual quality without project files or screenshots.
It may need adjustment for teams with different design system rules.

use_cases.title: Review a Generated Page
use_cases.description: Check a new page for spacing, typography, accessibility, motion, and layout issues before handoff.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design System Usage
use_cases.description: Guide component choices toward existing primitives, Tailwind defaults, and consistent interaction patterns.

use_cases.title: Improve AI Coding Output
use_cases.description: Apply a compact quality baseline when Claude, Codex, or Claude Code creates interface code.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for any UI task
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the baseline-ui rules to this UI task. Focus on spacing, accessibility, typography, layout, and obvious polish issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a component or page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baseline-ui to review this file. List each violation, why it matters, and one concrete fix for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Fix the Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI with baseline-ui, then make the smallest code changes needed to resolve the confirmed issues.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baseline-ui to audit this feature flow across components. Prioritize accessibility, interaction states, responsive layout, animation cost, and design consistency.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard page with several cards, filters, and loading states.
output: Violation: Loading states use generic spinners instead of structural skeletons near the content.
Why it matters: Users cannot understand what content is loading.
Fix: Replace the spinner with skeleton rows and card placeholders that match the final layout.

output_examples.input: Apply the baseline to an icon-only toolbar.
output: Violation: Several icon-only buttons do not expose an accessible name.
Why it matters: Screen reader users cannot identify the available actions.
Fix: Add clear aria-label values and keep keyboard focus states visible.

output_examples.input: Audit motion in a marketing-style settings screen.
output: Violation: The screen animates width and background color during hover feedback.
Why it matters: Layout and paint animation can feel unstable and perform poorly.
Fix: Use opacity or transform for short feedback, and respect reduced-motion preferences.

best_practices: Provide the relevant component or page file when asking for a review.
Ask for fixes after the review if you want code changes, not only findings.
Keep existing project primitives and theme tokens as the default source of truth.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a replacement for accessibility testing or visual regression checks.
Do not apply every suggestion blindly when your design system has stricter local rules.
Do not ask for decorative motion or gradients unless the product requirements explicitly need them.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews frontend UI work for spacing, hierarchy, typography, accessibility, animation, layout, performance, and basic design consistency.

faq.question: Does it edit code automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide edits when you ask for fixes, but its default file workflow reports violations and suggested changes.

faq.question: Which stacks does it fit best?
faq.answer: It fits Tailwind CSS and React-style component projects, especially projects using shared primitives.

faq.question: Can it replace a design system?
faq.answer: No. It is a baseline checklist that should follow your existing component library, tokens, and product standards.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill includes a documentation reference link, but it does not require fetching external content.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Ask Claude Code or Codex to apply baseline-ui during UI generation, review a file, or fix confirmed interface issues.
